setup_summary.text: Q3 2026 diluted EPS was $1.34 (about +10% y/y, about +16% ex the reserve build), with record net revenue of about $8B (+8.7%). Management raised full-year net revenue growth to 8–9% (from 5–7%) and full-year operating leverage to about 300bp (from 200bp). The Q4 report is due 2027-01-19 after the close, per the Finnhub calendar; EarningsWatcher has no confirmed date.

Guidance implies Q4 net revenue of about $8.0–8.1B, below the $8.16B consensus. I took Q3 tax-equivalent NII as about $4.49B (Q2 $4.387B x 1.023 linked-quarter). I backed out Q4 2025 NII (FTE) at about $4.31B (FY $16.765B less H1 $8.202B less a Q3 2025 figure of about $4.25B). Growing it 6–7% gives about $4.57–4.62B. Q4 2025 noninterest income is about $3.05B. Fees growing 13–14% give about $3.45–3.48B. Revenue is therefore about $8.02–8.10B before any securities losses, or about $8.0–8.1B allowing for some. Consensus is about $60–160M (0.7–2%) above the top of that range. The full-year guide (+8–9% on $28.656B, with H1 $15.0B and Q3 about $7.97B) implies a looser Q4 range of about $7.98–8.27B. Consensus of $8.16B sits inside it, in the upper half, at about +8.6% for the full year.

The fact sheet's consensus-implied growth rates use the wrong year-ago quarter. F.49 and F.51 compare Q4 2026 consensus with Q3 2025 ($7.33B revenue, $1.22 EPS). The correct base is Q4 2025: revenue of about $7.36B ($28.656B less H1 $13.962B less Q3 $7.33B) and EPS of about $1.26 ($4.62 less $2.14 less $1.22). Consensus is therefore about +10.8% on revenue and about +12.7% on EPS, not +11.3% and +16.5%. The bar is lower than the fact sheet implies on EPS, but revenue is still about 1pt above guide-implied growth of roughly 9–10%.

The $1.42 EPS consensus is essentially Q3's run-rate with the reserve build removed. Management said Q3 EPS ($1.34) carried a roughly $0.07 reserve-build impact. At about 1.555B shares and a roughly 21% tax rate, $0.07 is about $135–140M pre-tax. That is consistent with an initial provision on the purchased Amazon small-business card book, which the 10-Q says is expensed through provision for non-PCD purchases. Guidance implies Q4 revenue up about 1% q/q and expense up about 1.5–2% q/q, so pre-provision profit is roughly flat. $1.34 plus $0.07 is about $1.41, so $1.42 needs a near-zero reserve build and flat pre-provision profit. My range is $1.33–1.44, with a base of about $1.39 assuming a modest build.

The guide implies a sequential fee decline, which the market could misread. Q3 fees were about $3.5B (44% of about $7.97B revenue). Q4 fees at +13–14% on a Q4 2025 base of about $3.05B are about $3.45–3.48B, so about $30–70M lower q/q. BTIG explains about $25M of that (from $226M to about $200M). The rest comes from 'other' revenue normalizing to $120–150M after one-off Q3 gains, mortgage hurt by higher rates, and merchant near 0% growth. Legacy capital markets, corporate payments (+19% y/y) and trust partly offset.

Buybacks were paused in Q3 and management expects to restart within a quarter or two. CET1 was 10.8%, but AOCI-adjusted CET1 fell 30bp to 9.1%. The causes were $12B of RWA growth (heavy loan demand and the Amazon small-business card partnership) and a roughly 40bp hit from higher Treasury rates and wider spreads. TCE was stable at 6.6%. Earnings net of dividends added about 30bp. The CFO cited 33bp of capital generated after dividends, and the target remains a 70–75% payout. The restart timing depends on loan demand, rates and expected rule changes. The CEO said the restart does not rely on any Basel III endgame benefit.

Rates moved against the capital and mortgage lines after quarter-end. The Fed raised its target in September (first hike since July 2023) and held at 3.75–4% on October 28. The 10-year Treasury closed at 5.05% that day. Markets price one more 25bp hike in 2026 and further hikes into 2027. This supports asset repricing and the NIM story, but it is a headwind for AOCI, mortgage banking and CRE.

since_filing.text: The Q3 print (Oct 15) added to the 10-Q picture. EPS was $1.34 (+10% y/y), record revenue was about $8B (+8.7%, +6.4% adjusted for BTIG and securities losses), expenses grew 7.1% (2.0% ex-BTIG), and operating leverage was 240bp. Management lifted full-year revenue growth and operating-leverage guidance. This follows a Q2 10-Q showing EPS of $1.35 and revenue of $7.71B.

BTIG's first full quarter contributed $226M of fee revenue, and capital markets grew 69% y/y (10% legacy). Management guided to about $200M of BTIG fee revenue ahead and a target for capital markets to grow from 8% to 10% or more of total company revenue over the next three to five years. In Q2, capital markets was $512M, which included the contribution from BTIG after the June 1 close.

The Amazon small-business card portfolio was onboarded in Q3. It contributed about $900M to average loans and $1.7B to period-end loans, and it raised RWA and capital demand. The 10-Q credit card balance was $39.1B at June 30 for reference. A Q3 initial provision on this purchase is the likely source of the $0.07 reserve build. That inference rests on the 10-Q's policy statement, because no filing amount was available.

A new item since the 10-Q: management paused buybacks in Q3. At June 30 the 10-Q showed about $3,912M of the $5.0B authorization remaining, with 3.56M shares repurchased in Q2 at $56.39. The call says no new buyback has been done since, and an analyst referred to a disclosure 'a month or so' before the call.

USB filed the Series P Fixed Rate Reset Non-Cumulative Perpetual Preferred certificate on October 29. It closed the sale of 1,000,000 depositary shares (each 1/25th of a $25,000 preferred share, about $1.0B) on October 30. The 8-K gives no coupon or proceeds. The preferred adds to Tier 1 capital, not CET1. Series M ($750M, 4.00%) became callable from April 15, 2026, so a refinancing is a possibility but is unconfirmed.

On the rate backdrop, the Fed raised by 25bp on September 16 and held at 3.75–4% on October 28 in a hawkish hold with two dissenters favoring a hike. The 10-year closed at 5.05% on October 28, its first close above 5% since October 21 (5.13%). Markets price one more hike in 2026. USB's June 10-Q sensitivity table (NII +0.49% for -50bp, 0.00% for +50bp) pre-dates the hike. On the Q3 call management said it is moving toward asset sensitivity, with floating-rate loans at 30% of earning assets (22% four years ago).

Contradiction to flag: the fact-sheet consensus-implied growth rates (+11.3% revenue, +16.5% EPS) use Q3 2025 as the year-ago base and are mislabeled as Q4 growth. The correct Q4 2025 base is revenue of about $7.36B and EPS of about $1.26, so the correct growth rates are about +10.8% and +12.7%. The 10-Q figures themselves are not contradicted by the later call.

key_debates.question: Is the $8.16B / $1.42 consensus too high against the guidance?

bull.text: The Q3 EPS ex-reserve build was about $1.41. Guidance implies NIM up about 5bp, NII up 6–7%, and BTIG plus legacy capital markets holding up. If provision falls back to roughly net charge-offs, $1.42 is achievable with flat pre-provision profit. Management has raised guidance and described momentum.

bear.text: Line-item guidance bottom-up gives revenue of about $8.0–8.1B, about 1–2% below $8.16B. Fees fall sequentially as BTIG normalizes, 'other' reverts to $120–150M and mortgage is hit by rates. Expense growth is about 8%. Even a modest reserve build pushes EPS to about $1.37–1.39. The consensus snapshot has no revision history.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The Q4 release on 2027-01-19: reported revenue against $8.0–8.1B, the size of any reserve build, and Q4 fees against about $3.45–3.48B.

key_debates.question: When do buybacks restart, and how much does regulation matter?

bull.text: USB generated 33bp of capital after dividends in Q3, TCE was stable at 6.6%, and management says it has high confidence in the capital build. Management expects to restart over the next quarter or two. Basel III endgame is about a 5% RWA improvement and the CEO says USB is ready for Category II.

bear.text: AOCI-adjusted CET1 is 9.1% and fell 30bp in Q3, with RWA up $12B. The 10-year is still about 5%, loan growth is strong, and the restart depends on rates, loan demand and rule changes. USB is near the $700B four-quarter average asset threshold for Category II. Category II would bring AOCI recognition, full LCR/NSFR and annual stress tests.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The Q4 call's statement on repurchases (amount or timing), Q4 average assets against $700B, and any final Basel III endgame or tailoring rule in the fourth quarter.

key_debates.question: Can NIM rise toward 3% in 2027 as rates go up?

bull.text: Fixed-asset repricing of about $10B a quarter at +125bp, a mix shift to floating-rate C&I, CRE and card, improving funding mix and stable deposit and loan pricing. The CFO says mix and repricing are enough to offset competition on betas.

bear.text: Deposit betas are assumed at about 50% from the start, with a couple of hikes in the forecast. An analyst asked about residual liability sensitivity at the short end. Management said it aims to be neutral but has been shifting to asset sensitivity, and 'deposit competition may have something to say about that'. The curve and deposit competition are the open risks.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 NIM against the guided 2.89%, Q4 deposit-cost change versus the 7bp rise in Q3, and early 2027 NIM commentary.

key_debates.question: Is expense discipline holding after BTIG?

bull.text: Q3 expense grew 2.0% ex-BTIG, efficiency was about 56%, management has productivity runway from AI programs, and full-year operating leverage guidance rose by 100bp. The CFO targets the mid part of the mid-to-high-50s efficiency range.

bear.text: The Q4 guide of about +4% ex-BTIG is double Q3's 2.0%. Marketing (+34% in Q2), technology (+12.5% in Q2) and branch investment (rising to about $300M a year) are all growing faster than revenue ex-BTIG. Capital markets is a high-efficiency-ratio business, so more BTIG revenue raises the expense ratio.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 expense dollars and the ex-BTIG growth rate against about 4%, plus the 2027 operating leverage commentary at the fall conference and on the January call.

key_debates.question: How exposed is the credit book to higher rates, the new card portfolio and CRE?

bull.text: Q3 net charge-offs fell 2bp to 51bp, NPAs declined 1.6% q/q, card FICO bands have marginally improved, and management saw no change in consumer or commercial credit. At June 30 the allowance was 1.94% of loans and NPAs were down 15% year-to-date.

bear.text: The Amazon small business card portfolio contributed about $1.7B to Q3 period-end loans. CRE is the named watch item as rates rise. Criticized CRE loans were $3.4B at June 30, and NDFI balances ran off in Q3 because some deals did not hurdle. Card net charge-offs were 3.83% in Q2.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 net charge-offs, 90+ day card delinquency, CRE NPAs and criticized balances, and the Q4 reserve build against $0.07 in Q3.

scenarios.name: bear

description.text: Revenue of about $7.95–8.0B and EPS of about $1.30–1.34. Fees disappoint (mortgage, 'other' below $120M, BTIG below $200M), the deposit beta runs above the roughly 50% assumed as rates rise, and rate-driven reserve builds or CRE charge-offs push provision toward $650–700M. AOCI-adjusted CET1 stays near 9.1%, pushing out the buyback restart.

triggers: Provision above $650M or a rising reserve ratio
Buyback restart delayed beyond Q1 2027 or new regulatory burden

claim.text: Rate and AOCI risk. A 10-year near 5% already cost about 40bp of AOCI-adjusted CET1 in Q3 (to 9.1%). Further rate rises would delay the buyback restart, and USB's June 10-Q table showed only a roughly neutral +/-50bp NII profile. Higher rates also weigh on mortgage banking, which management expects to show limited growth in Q4.

Buyback and capital timing. Management paused repurchases in Q3, and the restart depends on loan demand, rates and rules. The Category II threshold ($700B four-quarter average assets) is close, with Q2 average assets at $694.7B, and the 10-Q does not say when USB will cross. Category II would bring AOCI recognition, full LCR and NSFR, and annual (rather than biennial) company-run stress tests.

BTIG integration and capital-markets volatility. BTIG is expected to contribute about $200M of fee revenue, and management calls capital markets a high-efficiency-ratio business. BTIG adds market risk (it joins market-risk capital calculations from Q3), and the risk factors flag that benefits may take longer or cost more than expected. Management targets capital markets growing from 8% to 10% or more of company revenue.

Credit risk from rapid card growth, the acquired Amazon portfolio and rising rates. Management says credit is unchanged and CRE is the watch item. CRE criticized balances were $3.4B at June 30 and NDFI balances ran off in Q3. Card net charge-offs were 3.83% in Q2 and the Amazon book adds $1.7B of balances with a limited performance record.

Payment-regulation risk. The Visa/Mastercard interchange injunctive settlement has a final approval hearing on November 16, 2026, and the 10-K flags credit card interest-rate caps and interchange limits as risks. Regulatory scrutiny, including fair-access inquiries from the OCC, is also ongoing.

Fee-mix and expense risk. 'Other' revenue (which included gains unique to Q3), mortgage and merchant are expected to be soft in Q4, and expenses are guided up about 8% y/y, or about 4% ex-BTIG. A miss on either could weigh on the positive operating leverage management guided for the full year (about 300bp).

questions_for_management.question: What explains the step-up in ex-BTIG expense growth from 2.0% in Q3 to about 4% in Q4? Is it incentive accruals, marketing, branch build-out or Amazon card launch costs?

why.text: The guide implies a sharp acceleration in core expense that nobody has explained, while full-year operating leverage was raised 100bp.

questions_for_management.question: How large was the initial provision on the Amazon small-business card portfolio, was it PCD or non-PCD, and should we assume Q4 provision tracks net charge-offs with no further build?

why.text: The reserve build cost about $0.07 in Q3, and $1.42 consensus is only reachable if it does not recur. USB's policy books non-PCD purchase allowance through provision at acquisition.

questions_for_management.question: Can you give a more specific buyback restart (Q4 or Q1) and quantify the capital build, including any RWA from Amazon, from loan growth and from the Category II transition?

why.text: The pause was new in Q3. Management said it would restart in the next quarter or two without counting on Basel relief, and the market will read the Q4 call for specifics.

questions_for_management.question: What is the Series P coupon and use of proceeds? Is it a refinancing of Series M or another series, or additional Tier 1 capital to support growth?

why.text: The 8-K does not disclose the coupon or proceeds. About $1.0B of preferred changes the preferred dividend line, and Series M ($750M at 4.00%) is already callable.

questions_for_management.question: What does the 3% NIM path in 2027 assume for deposit beta, the number of Fed hikes and fixed-asset repricing, and how does it change if the 10-year stays above 5%?

why.text: The Q4 NII guide and the 2027 NIM path depend on a roughly 50% initial beta and about $10B a quarter of repricing at +125bp, while rates and deposit competition are the stated risks.

questions_for_management.question: What is the seasonality and run-rate of BTIG fee revenue? Why is Q4 about $200M versus $226M in Q3, and what is the expected margin and compensation structure on that revenue?

why.text: About half of the guided Q4 fee growth of 13–14% y/y comes from BTIG, while 'other' revenue is expected to normalize to $120–150M after gains unique to Q3 and merchant is expected near 0%.

questions_for_management.question: What will you share at the fall capital markets conference on 2027 operating leverage, efficiency and capital markets disclosure?

why.text: Management committed to share more on capital markets strategy at a conference later this fall and said it is early in the 2027 budget process.

The 10-year yield at September 30 was not verified from a reliable source, so the change in AOCI since quarter-end cannot be sized. The status of final Basel III endgame or tailoring rules is based on management's expectation of rule changes in Q4 and older articles (December vote reported), not a confirmed event.
